$comment: S.F5a S4 (C-13, fold row 56) — the reseatToSpring-vs-decayRest release-seam decision, MEASURED (bench/spring-tick.bench.ts: `reseatToSpring · 600 interruptions` vs `decayRest · 600 releases`). C-13 forces the speculative LIGHT export `reseatToSpring` to a decision INSIDE S (no carry): wire the winner into the fling/release path fold row 56 names, OR record the measured reason the current shape stays. VERDICT: RETAIN-both — the two are DISTINCT motion models, not throughput substitutes, and the drag/decay release seam already consumes each where its model fits.
ratioMeaning: decayRest is ~22x faster per event than reseatToSpring — because it computes something different, NOT because it is a cheaper way to do the same thing. decayRest is the O(1) frictional-glide PROJECTION x0 + v0/k (one divide + one add, no object); reseatToSpring finite-differences a two-sample VelocityProbe and CONSTRUCTS a fresh velocity-continuous SpringProgress (an allocation + closed-form seed per event). The gap IS the evidence they are not substitutes.
rationale: decayRest (physics/decay.ts) is the O(1) targetless PROJECTION of where a release coasts to under friction. The release seam (orchestration/drag/draggable.ts:handleUp, snap branch) uses it to pick the nearest snap target WITHOUT running any loop. reseatToSpring cannot replace it: reseatToSpring produces a live settling object, not a projected scalar.

reseatToSpring (physics/spring/solver/reseat.ts) is the velocity-CONTINUOUS spring CONSTRUCTOR for the keyframe-stream interruption seam (PHYS-B2): the engine interp path carries only a POSITION at interruption (no analytic velocity, no pre-existing spring), so a fresh SpringProgress must be built from the finite-differenced velocity. decayRest cannot replace it: decayRest yields no settling trajectory.

The drag/decay release seam already consumes BOTH correctly and does NOT wire reseatToSpring: the draggable OWNS a persistent spring (this.spring) and re-seats it IN PLACE via spring.reset(x, v) — zero-alloc, preserving the spring identity the rAF draw loop reads. Wiring reseatToSpring there would ALLOCATE a fresh SpringProgress per release and sever that identity. The measured 22x cost gap (alloc-bearing construct vs O(1) projection) is exactly why the per-release path uses in-place reset, and why reseatToSpring's home is the no-pre-existing-spring interruption case, not the draggable's persistent-spring hot path.

reseatToSpring is RETAINED (not stripped): it is the documented, gated (proof:spring-blend-weight PHYS-B2) velocity-continuous interruption primitive and a named agent-surface export (scripts/lib/agent-surface.mjs). It is unconsumed INTERNALLY by intent — its consumer is the external keyframe-interruption caller, not an in-library seam.
